text:
Maya: Heads-up — primary couldn't unblock their flight, we'll have a coverage gap for tonight's overnight shift starting 22:00 UTC. Need a short-notice primary or shadow. Holiday weekend so pulls are rough.

Jon: Ugh, ok. How long is the gap? I can take the first 4 hours if that helps.

Maya: Thanks Jon. Gap is 22:00-06:00 UTC (8h). Ideally we want a primary + secondary for the first 6 hours then hand off to APAC shadow.

Tess: I can be secondary for first 3 hrs then hand to Sam (if Sam is available). What's the current SLO/customer impact?

Maya: OpsBot reported an uptick in 504s to model-serving in us-east-1 earlier but it stabilized. This is precautionary: we expect higher traffic because of the holiday promo. If we get pagers we need to follow the "model-serving - perf" runbook. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving-perf

OpsBot: :rotating_light: Alert created (INC-2026-117). Monitored service: model-serving-prod-us-east-1. Metric: 99th latency > 1200ms. Current status: recovered.

Jon: Copy. Maya — do we want me to be primary on-call in rotation (handle page and do mitigation) or just primary for bridging until someone fully takes the overnight? I can do full primary for first 4h.

Maya: Full primary would be ideal. You'll own pages, decision on rollback/fallback, and on-call checklist entries. Tess + Sam as secondary/shadow. If anything looks like data exfil or security, escalate immediately to eng-security.

Tess: Quick checklist snippet for anyone jumping in (pasted from runbook):
```
1) Check grafana dashboard: Model-serving > us-east-1 > request-latency
2) Validate autoscaler logs: `kubectl -n model get hpa`
3) If latency spike > 2x baseline, enable fallback model variant:
   - POST /admin/fallback?pool=gen2-quant
4) Notify support & update status page template
```

Alice: I can open the status page template if we start getting customer reports. Tag me on #support and I'll post updates.

Sam: I'm happy to take the APAC shadow from 02:00 UTC onward (so I can overlap with Jon/Tess). If Jon needs relief at 02:00, we can swap.

Jon: Sounds good. One more: what about the dedicated capacity timeout we hit last month? Any quick mitigations pre-approved?

Maya: Pre-approved quick mitigations in runbook: revert last config change (if within 30m), scale up pool via infra playbook, and enable degraded-mode routing to reduce token budget per request. Commands below: 
```
# scale up pool (requires infra sudo)
ssh infra@jump
infra> infractl pools scale --name=redwood-gen2-us-east --replicas=+2

# enable degraded routing (app team toggle)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" https://internal-api/routing/degraded?enable=true
```

Tess: If Jon's primary, I'll post the handover checklist and keep monitoring alerts. I'll also monitor the eval suite for any quality regressions when fallback model gets used.

Maya: Ok final plan: Jon = primary 22:00-02:00 UTC (full), Tess = secondary 22:00-01:00 UTC (monitor + handoff), Sam = APAC shadow 02:00-06:00 UTC, Alice = status page & customer comms. If anyone can't make it, shout now. Otherwise we'll do formal handshake before 22:00.

Jon: I have it. Will update rotation and set Slack status + Pager on. :thumbsup:

Tess: Will DM Jon the runbook shortcuts and my monitoring playbook.

Alice: I'll prep the status template now and keep Slack channel open.

OpsBot: :white_check_mark: Handoff recorded in oncall-runbook-log (entry id: 2026-117-226789). Participants: Jon, Tess, Sam, Alice.

Maya: Thanks all. If we get a page, follow the runbook and tag me if you need escalation. Good luck and sorry for the holiday ask.

Sam: On standby — ping me at 01:45 UTC for a handover check.

Jon: Will ping 21:45 UTC for final handshake and confirm Pager routing.

Tess: :rocket:
